summary: Dedicated UI UX designers and embedded design teams on a monthly plan.
abstract: Companies hire UI UX designers from ui-ux.agency, the design team of tkxel, when they need design capacity faster than recruiting allows. A team of 2 to 5 dedicated designers in user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) starts in 1 to 2 weeks, works inside the client's sprints and costs $15,000 to $40,000 per month on a monthly plan, with no recruiting fees and a 30-day notice period.

sections.h2: Why hire UI UX designers from an agency?
sections.answer: Companies hire UI UX designers from an agency to add senior design capacity in weeks instead of months, without the cost and risk of a permanent hire. The designers work as part of your team while the agency handles hiring, training and cover.
sections.body: Recruiting one senior product designer takes 2 to 4 months and a recruiter fee. An agency team is ready in 1 to 2 weeks, brings research, UX and UI skills together, and keeps working when one person takes leave. It suits product teams with a growing roadmap, a launch date or a redesign that needs more hands than the current team has. For a fixed-scope project instead of ongoing capacity, see our product design agency work.

sections.h2: Which roles can you hire from our UI UX design team?
sections.answer: You can hire UI UX designers in 5 roles, alone or as a team:

items.title: Product designer.
items.body: Owns features end to end, from flows to final screens. To hire one on their own, see hire a product designer.

items.title: UX researcher.
items.body: Runs interviews, usability tests and surveys, and turns findings into design priorities.

items.title: UI designer.
items.body: Designs final screens, icons and motion, and keeps the visual language consistent.

items.title: Design system designer.
items.body: Builds and maintains components, tokens and documentation with your engineers.

items.title: Design lead.
items.body: Sets direction, reviews work and connects design with product and engineering leadership.

sections.h2: Should you hire a UI designer or a UX designer?
sections.answer: Hire a UX designer when users struggle to finish tasks, and hire a UI designer when the product works but looks dated or inconsistent. Many teams need both, which is why we staff them as one UI UX team.

sections.h2: How do you hire UI UX designers from ui-ux.agency?
sections.answer: Hiring UI UX designers from us takes 4 steps and 1 to 2 weeks from the first call to the first day of work.

items.title: Scoping call (day 1)
items.body: We discuss your product, roadmap, team and the skills you need.

items.title: Team proposal (days 2–4)
items.body: We send profiles and portfolios of the designers who fit, plus a monthly price.

items.title: Interviews (days 5–8)
items.body: You meet the designers and choose who joins your team.

items.title: Onboarding (days 8–14)
items.body: Designers get access to your tools, meet the team and start on the first sprint.

sections.h2: What is included when you hire UI UX designers from us?
sections.answer: Every plan to hire UI UX designers from us includes 4 things beyond design hours.

items.title: Design lead review

items.title: Tools and licenses

sections.h2: How much does it cost to hire UI UX designers?
sections.answer: Hiring a dedicated UI UX design team from us costs $15,000 to $40,000 per month for 2 to 5 designers. Team size and seniority set the monthly price.
sections.body: A product designer and a UI designer working full time sit near $15,000 per month. A team with a design lead, a researcher and three designers for a large platform sits near $40,000 per month. Teams that need a one-off project instead, such as a SaaS product redesign, get a fixed quote. Compare every option in the UI UX design cost guide.

sections.answer: Answers to common questions from teams that want to hire UI UX designers.

faqs.q: Can I hire one UI UX designer instead of a team?
faqs.a: Yes. A single dedicated designer is possible; we still include a weekly review by a design lead.

faqs.q: Do your designers work in US time zones?
faqs.a: Yes. Every designer overlaps at least 4 hours with US Eastern time, and many teams choose full overlap. Teams on Mountain Time can see how the 2-hour gap works on our UX agency Denver page, and Central Time teams can read how remote UX work with Minneapolis teams runs.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum contract length?
faqs.a: No. Plans run month to month with 30 days notice.
